TdT+ cells are increased in lymphoid tissues of patients with Castleman disease and angioimmunoblatic T-cell lymphoma, and in lymphoid tissues in association with follicullar dendritic cell tumors.
indolent TdT+ T lymphoblastic proliferations occur in association with CD and AITL, and are increased in lymph node biopsies of patients with CD compared with other lymphomas or reactive nodes.

TdT+ thymocytes are increased in Castlema disease, in Castlema disease in association with a follicular cell dendritic cell tumor, and in angiolimmunoblastic lymphoma, and that these populations are not increased in other hematolymphoid tumors or carcinomas.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a rare subset of T-lymphoid proliferations, which may have prognostic and therapeutic implications.
the identification of a population of non-neopastic TdT+ T-cells that are increased in specific hematologic diseases and not in nonhematolmphoid tumors.
identifying a subset of TdT+ T lymphocytes that are not associated with a neoplastic T-cell population and are increased in patients with specific hematologic disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TdT+ cells are not neoplastic but rather are reactive in nature and may be seen in association with specific hematologic malignancies.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

indolent TdT+ T-cell proliferations are increased in patients with CD, CD in association with a follicular dentritic cell tumor, and AITl, and these indolent proliferations should be distinguished from neoplastic TdT + T-lymphomas.
TdT+ lymphocytes are increased in CD, CD associated with follicular dendrite cell tumors, and angioimmunoloblastic T-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
TdT+ lymphoblastic populations are significantly increased in lymph nodes with CD or AITL, and that these populations may be a marker for CD or AIT L.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the identification of TdT+ T lymphoblasts in lymphoid tissues should prompt consideration of the possibility of indolent proliferation, which is distinct from T-lymphoma.
the presence of TdT+ T lymphocytes in extrathymically localized lymphoid tissues does not always indicate T-lymphoblatic lymphoma.
